subject: Hosted API — backlog-driven latency spike and p95/p99 regression
messages:
From: Emma Barnes <emma@finlytics.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: apiops@finlytics.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency spike — p95 / p99 up across hosted API (Finlytics production)

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a major latency regression in production at ~07:40 PT. P95 jumped from ~320ms to >1.2s and p99 is spiking past 3s. Error rate is also elevated (5xxs clustering around the same window). This is impacting our realtime scoring pipelines; we've queued up backlogged requests and some timeouts are cascading downstream.

Attached are a few traces and our API request histogram for the last 2 hours. Can your team confirm root cause / ETA for mitigation? Any workaround on your side to reduce latency while you investigate would be hugely appreciated.

Thanks,
Emma Barnes
Head of Platform — Finlytics

Attachment: finlytics-traces-20270423.zip (zip, 1.9MB)

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 / p99 up across hosted API (Finlytics production)

Forwarding Finlytics traces and hist. TL;DR: early signs point to sustained request buildup in the batching queue for the multi-tenant host pool handling Finlytics traffic. That increased queue depth is inflating batch latencies and amplifying p95/p99.

Marissa / Dylan — can you triage the serving-side traces? Look at batching window, worker utilization, and KV cache hit rates for the 07:30–08:10 window. If capacity saturation, suggest short-term mitigations: 1) reduce batch_window_ms from 20->5 for that pool, 2) raise worker_count by +2 nodes, or 3) route Finlytics to the adjacent warm pool if compatible.

I'll loop in Finlytics once we have a recommended immediate action.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — p95 / p99 up across hosted API (Finlytics production)

Quick triage notes (07:30–08:10):
- Worker CPU/GPU not saturated overall, but one host pool showed sustained queue depth growth (avg queue depth for pool A: 42 -> 190) and longer batching windows observed in traces.
- KV cache hit-rate dipped ~11% at spike time; we saw increased cold-starts for attention cache on several shards.
- Batching aggregator logs show a delayed flush event pattern — flush thresholds were being hit at larger batch sizes which increased per-batch service time.

Immediate action taken at 08:40: - reduced batch_window_ms from 20ms -> 6ms for pool A (testing), - scaled pool A +2 workers (hot-add). Initial telemetry shows p95 moving from ~1.25s -> ~520ms within 4 minutes; p99 still elevated at ~1.9s.

Next steps: continue telemetry, consider temporarily lowering max_batch_size for Finlytics to limit worst-case per-batch latency, and prepare a fallback to route the account to dedicated capacity if regressions persist.

— Dylan
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Barnes <emma@finlytics.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — hosted API impact and live mitigations

Hi Emma — quick update from the ops side.

We reduced the batching window and scaled the pool. You should see improvements in p95; our dashboards show ~60% reduction in tail latency within 6 minutes of the change. We're continuing to monitor p99 and error-rate clusters.

We are also preparing a short-lived routing rule that will divert Finlytics traffic to a neighboring warm pool that has capacity available; this will be enabled if p99 doesn't fall below 1s in the next 30 minutes. We'll confirm before flipping any routing.

We appreciate the traces you provided — they helped us pin the timing. We'll keep you posted every 30 minutes and share the post-incident notes.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Hosted API
Attachment: p95-p99-timeseries-20270423.csv (csv, 120KB)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — suggested exec note and SLA ask

Soojin / Laura — FYI for leadership thread. Customer is asking for clear ETA and possible SLA credit given impact to their realtime scoring. Recommend:
1) Prepare an executive one-pager with timeline, root cause (batch backlog due to transient cache coldness + mis-tuned flush), mitigation steps, and next steps (code fix to better prioritize small-latency traffic + autoscale rule for queue depth).
2) Offer a temporary credits package if Finlytics demonstrates measurable business impact tied to our service regression (coordinate with finance & legal).
3) Post-incident: rollout smarter batching heuristics (dynamic batch window) and a per-account routing knob to avoid multi-tenant co-tenancy hotspots.

I'll draft the exec note; Soojin, can you take lead on communication with Finlytics for the SLA ask? Laura — please prepare the support-side timeline and capture customer impact details for finance review.

— Jonas
Head of Ops Reliability

From: soojin.lee@redwood.com <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Barnes <emma@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency spike — hosted API impact and next steps

Emma —

Thanks again for the fast traces. Short update and next steps:
- What we saw: transient queue buildup in pool A caused larger-than-expected batch formation. This was compounded by a drop in KV cache hit-rate on a subset of shards (coldness) which increased per-request work and delayed flush thresholds. Net effect: p95/p99 regression and a backlog of requests briefly.
- Immediate mitigation: we lowered batch window and increased worker count which reduced p95 from ~1.25s to ~420–520ms and reduced error spikes. We did not flip routing to the adjacent pool because mitigations were effective, but the routing option remains if needed.
- Next steps we are executing: (a) post-incident RCA including traces (we'll share within 48 hours), (b) short-term config: per-account max_batch_size and dynamic batch_window can be toggled for your account to reduce future tail risk, (c) engineering story to add queue-depth autoscaling and dynamic batching heuristics to prevent similar buildup.

We will also begin preparing an executive incident brief and coordinate with finance about credits if the incident caused measurable downstream business impact for Finlytics. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with priority.

If you'd like a 30-min bridge to walk through the timeline and mitigation choices, I can schedule for today.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA-exception-request-brief.pdf (pdf, 45KB)
